newsitem.title: FRANCE: France to scrap nuclear fast breeder - Jospin.
newsitem.headline: France to scrap nuclear fast breeder - Jospin.

text.p: French Socialist Prime Minister Lionel Jospin said on Thursday he would scrap the fault-prone Superphenix nuclear fast-breeder, describing it as too costly and of doubtful value.

The announcement, made in Jospin's first policy statement to the National Assembly, was a victory for Greens leader Dominique Voynet, who became environment minister after the left's victory in June 1 elections and has denounced the reactor as "stupid financial waste" .
The controversial 1,200 megawatt, 60-billion-franc ($10.5 billion) plant built 20 years ago near the Alpine town of Grenoble is the ecologists' bete noire.

"If nuclear industry is a major asset for our country, it cannot be outside democratic rules nor pursue projects whose cost is excessive and whose success is uncertain: this is why the fast-breeder known as Superphenix will be dropped," Jospin said.
Superphenix, 51 percent owned by state utility Electricite de France, with Italy's ENEL and a Dutch-German-Belgian consortium as partners, was constructed to produce more plutonium than it consumed.

But it has been on line for only 30 months and fed the electricity grid for only 10 months. The government downgraded it in 1994 to a research reactor working at reduced power as a tool of research into disposing of nuclear waste.
Environmentalists describe it as a dangerous dinosaur, although nuclear experts say it is as safe as any other plant.
Its supporters have warned of the high cost of an early closure for majority owner Electricite de France, and of dire losses of jobs and tax income for the region.
A disputed 1995 government study said it would cost up to 20 billion francs ($3 billion) to close the plant two decades ahead of the scheduled date of 2020.

The reactor was due to restart this month after shutting down six months ago because of more faults. But the Council of State, France's top administrative court, cancelled its 1994 authorisation to operate as a research reactor.
The council ruled that the procedure for transforming the power plant into a research prototype was flawed and required a new public inquiry.
Former conservative prime minister Alain Juppe was believed to have wanted to keep the plant operating. But his defeat in the June 1 elections sounded Superphenix's death knell.
